config.title: Build websocket reconnect manager

intro.title: Build websocket reconnect manager
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a WebSocket reconnect manager to handle dropped connections automatically. You will learn how to use JavaScript's WebSocket API to establish real-time communication with a server. The core programming concept involves managing state and event handlers to detect disconnections and trigger reconnection attempts. You'll work with timers, event listeners, and conditional logic to create a resilient connection that recovers from failures. This project introduces you to building reliable network applications in JavaScript.
intro.usecase: WebSocket reconnect managers are essential in real-time applications where persistent connections are critical. In live trading dashboards, they maintain price feed updates during network fluctuations. Chat applications like Slack use them to ensure message delivery when users switch networks. Collaborative editing tools like Google Docs implement reconnection logic to sync changes after temporary disconnections. Video conferencing platforms rely on these managers to restore streams when internet connectivity drops briefly.

objectives: Construct a WebSocket connection with configurable URL and protocols
Implement automatic reconnection logic with exponential backoff
Initialize state variables to track connection status and retry attempts
Bind event handlers for WebSocket open, message, error, and close events
Control reconnection behavior based on connection state and error types
Integrate reconnection management into a functional WebSocket client
Manipulate connection parameters to test different reconnection scenarios

steps.title: Import WebSocket API and create connection state variables
steps.instruction: Import the WebSocket API and create variables to track connection state, reconnect attempts, and WebSocket instance.
steps.hint: The WebSocket API is built into JavaScript, so you don't need to import it. Just declare variables to store the WebSocket instance, connection status, and reconnect count.
steps.seedCode:
// Import the WebSocket API and create connection state variables

// Declare variables for WebSocket instance, connection status, and reconnect attempts
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have variables ready to manage WebSocket connection state.
successCriteria: Variables for WebSocket instance, connection status, and reconnect attempts are declared.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've set up the foundation for tracking WebSocket connection state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've declared variables for the WebSocket instance, connection status, and reconnect attempts.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to declare variables to store the WebSocket instance, track whether we're connected, and count reconnect attempts.

steps.title: Create WebSocket connection function
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'connectWebSocket' that takes a URL parameter and initializes a new WebSocket connection.
steps.hint: Define a function that accepts a URL string and creates a new WebSocket instance with it.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named connectWebSocket is defined with a URL parameter and creates a WebSocket instance.
successCriteria: The connectWebSocket function is created and accepts a URL parameter to initialize a WebSocket connection.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the connectWebSocket function that will establish WebSocket connections.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your function is named 'connectWebSocket' and accepts a URL parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't quite right. Create a function named 'connectWebSocket' that takes a URL parameter.

steps.title: Add WebSocket onopen event handler
steps.instruction: Inside the connectWebSocket function, add an onopen event handler to the WebSocket instance that updates the connection status when the connection opens successfully.
steps.hint: Assign a function to the ws.onopen property that sets a variable or logs a success message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The connectWebSocket function now includes an onopen handler that responds to successful WebSocket connections.
successCriteria: The connectWebSocket function contains a WebSocket instance with an onopen event handler assigned.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the onopen event handler to handle successful WebSocket connections.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've assigned a function to the ws.onopen property inside the connectWebSocket function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The onopen event handler is missing or incorrectly placed. It should be inside the connectWebSocket function and assigned to the WebSocket instance.

steps.title: Add WebSocket onmessage event handler
steps.instruction: Inside the connectWebSocket function, add an onmessage event handler to the WebSocket instance that logs incoming messages to the console.
steps.hint: Use ws.onmessage = function(event) { console.log('Message received:', event.data); } or an arrow function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The connectWebSocket function now includes an onmessage handler that logs received messages.
successCriteria: The WebSocket instance has an onmessage event handler that logs the message data to the console.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the onmessage handler. This allows your WebSocket to process incoming messages from the server.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the onmessage handler is properly attached to the WebSocket instance and logs the message data.
steps.feedbackWrong: The onmessage handler is missing or incorrect. Remember to assign a function to ws.onmessage that logs the event.data.

steps.title: Add WebSocket onerror event handler
steps.instruction: Inside the connectWebSocket function, add an onerror event handler to the WebSocket instance that logs an error message to the console.
steps.hint: You can assign a function to ws.onerror that receives an event parameter and logs the error.
steps.expectedOutcome: The connectWebSocket function will now handle WebSocket errors by logging them to the console.
successCriteria: The connectWebSocket function includes an onerror event handler that logs an error message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added an error handler to the WebSocket connection.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the onerror handler logs an error message to the console.
steps.feedbackWrong: The onerror event handler is missing or not properly logging an error message.

steps.title: Add WebSocket onclose event handler
steps.instruction: Inside the connectWebSocket function, add an onclose event handler to the WebSocket instance that triggers reconnection logic when the connection closes.
steps.hint: Add ws.onclose = () => { ... } inside the connectWebSocket function after the other event handlers.
steps.expectedOutcome: The connectWebSocket function now includes an onclose event handler that will execute when the WebSocket connection closes.
successCriteria: The connectWebSocket function contains an onclose event handler attached to the WebSocket instance.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the onclose event handler. This will be triggered when the WebSocket connection closes, allowing you to implement reconnection logic in the next steps.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added the onclose event handler inside the connectWebSocket function and attached it to the WebSocket instance.
steps.feedbackWrong: The onclose event handler is missing. Add ws.onclose = () => { ... } inside the connectWebSocket function to handle connection closure events.

steps.title: Create reconnect function with exponential backoff
steps.instruction: Create a function named reconnectWebSocket that takes a URL parameter and implements exponential backoff logic for reconnection attempts.
steps.hint: Define a function that calculates a delay that increases with each attempt (e.g., using Math.pow) and calls setTimeout to attempt reconnection after that delay.
steps.expectedOutcome: A reconnectWebSocket function is defined that will handle reconnection attempts with increasing delays.
successCriteria: The reconnectWebSocket function is created with a URL parameter and contains logic for exponential backoff delay calculation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the reconnect function with exponential backoff logic.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the function, but make sure it includes the exponential backoff calculation (like using Math.pow) and a setTimeout call.
steps.feedbackWrong: The reconnectWebSocket function isn't properly defined. Create a function that takes a URL parameter and implements exponential backoff for reconnection attempts.

steps.title: Add maximum reconnect attempts limit
steps.instruction: Inside the reconnectWebSocket function, add a variable to track the maximum reconnect attempts and check if the current attempt exceeds it before attempting to reconnect.
steps.hint: You can define a constant like maxReconnectAttempts and compare it with the current reconnect attempt count.
steps.expectedOutcome: The reconnectWebSocket function will include logic to prevent infinite reconnection attempts by checking against a maximum limit.
successCriteria: The reconnectWebSocket function contains a maximum reconnect attempts constant and a conditional check to stop reconnection when the limit is reached.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a maximum reconnect attempts limit to prevent infinite reconnection loops.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've defined a maximum attempts constant and added a conditional check before attempting to reconnect.
steps.feedbackWrong: The maximum reconnect attempts limit hasn't been properly implemented. Review the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Create connection manager object with public methods
steps.instruction: Create a connection manager object named 'websocketManager' that exposes three public methods: connect, disconnect, and send.
steps.hint: Define an object with methods that call your existing functions or handle WebSocket operations. The connect method should take a URL parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: A websocketManager object is created with three method placeholders.
successCriteria: The websocketManager object exists and has connect, disconnect, and send methods defined.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the connection manager object with the required methods. This encapsulates WebSocket management into a reusable interface.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created an object, but it's missing some required methods. Make sure to include connect, disconnect, and send methods.
steps.feedbackWrong: The connection manager object wasn't created correctly. Create an object named 'websocketManager' with connect, disconnect, and send methods.

steps.title: Test the WebSocket reconnect manager
steps.instruction: Add a test function that simulates connection loss and recovery by calling the websocketManager's connect method with a test WebSocket URL, then manually triggering the onclose event to test reconnection.
steps.hint: Create a function named testReconnectManager that calls websocketManager.connect with a dummy URL, then simulates a connection closure by calling ws.onclose manually.
steps.expectedOutcome: A test function is added that will allow you to verify the reconnect manager works by simulating a connection loss scenario.
successCriteria: The testReconnectManager function is defined, calls websocketManager.connect with a test URL, and simulates triggering the onclose event.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added a test function that simulates connection loss and recovery. This will help verify the reconnect manager's functionality.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the test function, but make sure it calls websocketManager.connect with a test URL and simulates the onclose event to trigger reconnection.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test function is missing or doesn't properly simulate connection loss and recovery. Ensure it calls websocketManager.connect and triggers the onclose event.
